findings.reason: the plan must either reconcile the two grammars explicitly (and pin the preserved behaviour of `ledger`/`evidence` with a test) or drop the "one regular expression" claim, because the merge is only sound if the three readers really share one grammar and they do not.
findings.text: `routing._SECTION_IDENTITY` (`^(?:§|#)?\s*(?:s(?:ection)?[\s.-]*)?(\d+(?:[.-]\d+)*)$`) accepts hyphenated numeric continuations, while `ledger.normalize_section` (`reckon/ledger.py:206`) and `evidence._section_key` (`reckon/evidence.py:52`) match only the dotted form `\d+(?:\.\d+)*`; §16 asserts the three "share ... the one regular expression that recognises a section spelling", but they do not, so hoisting one shared regex silently changes a reader on input like `5-1` (routing → `s5-1`, ledger/evidence → unchanged), and the plan states no rule for which grammar wins or a test that the losing reader's output is preserved

findings.reason: §16 and §17 have mutually inconsistent done-whens and the census that is supposed to prove consolidation cannot see the parser §16 grows; the design must either route the prose parser's heading handling through `_StructuredSectionSpanParser`/`plan_headings`, or widen the census definition to catch `HTMLParser` heading handlers and state the shared heading set.
findings.text: `_AuthoredProseParser` (which §16 extends to record the enclosing section element's attributes and call `section_record_id` "at every heading") already tracks headings itself via `elif tag == "h2"` in `handle_starttag`, a second heading handler over the same document beside `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` (`reckon/_plan_html.py:44`) that §17 makes the one owner of section enumeration and boundary; §17's heading-walk census rule is specified to report only `find_all`/`find`/`select` on heading tags, `<h2` regex literals and `_H2_OPEN_RE`, none of which match an `HTMLParser.handle_starttag` heading check, so §17's done-when ("the heading-walk rule, run at the head, reports only the parser in `reckon/_plan_html.py`") passes while a second heading walk survives — and the two disagree on the heading set, since §17 generalises the span parser to h1–h6 while the prose parser stays h2

rubric_items.deep_module: a finding — §16 hoists one section-identity derivation to `reckon/_plan_html.py` and asserts the three spelling readers "share ... the one regular expression", but two of them encode different grammars today.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — two parsers re-implement heading/section-boundary recognition over the same document, and the census §17 relies on to prove "every heading walk ... is rewritten" is defined so that it cannot see the second one.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1476, cli_options 317, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; §16 declares net zero and names the retired public `legacy` flag on `plan_fingerprint`, §17 declares net +1 naming the added `plan_headings` and the moved `landed_section_ids`, §18 declares net zero naming the retired private `_plan_remaining_sections` and the reused `plan-review-missing` refusal family.
rubric_items.reuse_search: pass — the implementable sections (§16–§18) cite and extend machinery that exists: `_AuthoredProseParser` and `read_plan_review`/`list_plan_reviews` in `reckon/crew/plan_review.py`, `_StructuredSectionSpanParser` plus the AST census (`read_trees`, `definitions`, `_staged_writes`) in `reckon/_plan_html.py` and `reckon/interface_counts.py`, and `roadmap.implementable_sections` (`reckon/roadmap.py:106`); each is present as claimed.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the coverage predicate is explicitly shown not to be a wrapper over `read_plan_review` (it joins the outstanding-section set to the union of stored section digests), and §18 extends `roadmap.implementable_sections` rather than forking `promotion._plan_remaining_sections`.
